# Cost-Based Operating Points (generated by cost_analysis.py)

Computed from PERSISTED predictions (amendment A7); no model was refit.

## Assumptions, stated as assumptions

- Review capacity is a fraction of scored transactions. A bank sets it from analyst headcount, so it is a policy input, not a property of the model.
- The cost ratio (missed fraud versus false positive) is SWEPT over [20, 50, 100] rather than fixed, because its true value is institution-specific.
- Expected cost is reported RELATIVE to alerting nothing, so only differences between arms are interpreted.
- ULB spans two days, so these are capacity-shaped comparisons, not a deployment forecast.

## Expected cost per 1,000 transactions, relative to alerting nothing

Lower is better. Cost = false_positives + ratio * missed_frauds, at the 0.1% budget.

|---|---|---|---|
| catboost/full | -19.83 | -49.59 | -99.20 |

## Per-seed paired BCa intervals (prereg 9; closes the Sprint 4 OPEN item)

Identical stratified resample indices on both arms' prediction vectors.

Hardware predictions were not persisted in Sprint 4 (Dirac-3 weights; re-deriving them would cost metered seconds), so this runs on the EXACT PROXY of the same config. Sprint 4 measured hardware minus that proxy at -0.0010 AUPRC with the CI containing zero, so the substitution is supported by evidence rather than assumed.
